leased-hotel-remaining-lease-term-paybac.title: 租赁物业做酒店，剩余租期怎样约束回本和估值？
leased-hotel-remaining-lease-term-paybac.titleEn: Running a Hotel in Leased Premises: How Does the Remaining Lease Term Constrain Payback and Valuation?
leased-hotel-remaining-lease-term-paybac.description: 租来的物业做酒店，改造投入要在可执行的剩余租期内收回，续租只作情景、不作基准。本文按《民法典》和租赁司法解释拆开合同租期与可执行租期、续租选择权与优先承租、可带走设备与附合装修，给出一张四列租期约束测算表，并说明剩余年限怎样限制收购或转让时的出价。
leased-hotel-remaining-lease-term-paybac.descriptionEn: When a hotel operates in leased premises, the renovation investment has to be recovered within the enforceable remaining lease term. A renewal belongs in a scenario, not in the base case.
leased-hotel-remaining-lease-term-paybac.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 租来的物业做酒店，改造投入要在可执行的剩余租期里收回，续租只能放进情景测算，不能当作基准。估值也受同一条约束：只买经营权、不买房屋时，买方愿付的价格，不应高于这段年限里能拿到的现金流减去到期复原费用。合同上写的剩余年数，只是起点。
这件事常被做反。投委会先算回收期，再看租约够不够；或者听出租人说一句“到期肯定续给你”，就把续租后的年份也算进去。出租人的口头答复、意向书和新闻里的表态，都只是过程材料，写进合同的条款才算数。
## 合同上写的租期，为什么不等于能用的年数？
先拆开两个概念。合同约定租期，是租赁合同写明的起止日期。可执行的剩余租期，是从今天算起，到承租人可能被迫离场的最早日期为止的年数。后者往往更短。
第一道上限来自法律。《民法典》第七百零五条规定：“租赁期限不得超过二十年。超过二十年的，超过部分无效。”期满可以续订，但续订的期限自续订之日起也不得超过二十年。合同写三十年，测算只能按二十年计。
第二道来自合同。华住集团在2025年度报告里写明，其租约通常约定，在一定的法律或事实条件下可以提前终止。征收、出租人收回、重新开发这类条款一旦可能触发，可执行租期就截到那一天。
第三道来自出租人自己的权利。《最高人民法院关于审理城镇房屋租赁合同纠纷案件具体应用法律若干问题的解释》（2020年修正，下称租赁司法解释）第二条规定，出租人就未取得建设工程规划许可证或者未按许可证建设的房屋订立的租赁合同无效，一审法庭辩论终结前补办的除外。第十四条规定，房屋在出租前已设立抵押权，因抵押权人实现抵押权发生所有权变动的，除另有约定外，承租人请求新的所有人继续履行原租约，得不到支持。
出租人如果自己也是租来的，即俗称的二房东，《民法典》第七百一十七条规定，转租期限超过其剩余租赁期限的部分，对原出租人不具有法律约束力，另有约定的除外。华住在年报风险因素里也写到，部分出租人未能提供房屋所有权证或土地使用权证，相关租约可能被认定无效，酒店可能需要搬迁。
## 续租条款、优先承租和不定期租赁，各管多少？
合同里与“续”有关的写法，力度差别很大。承租人可以单方决定续租、租金按约定公式确定的，叫续租选择权，最接近确定。只写“双方协商续签”的，等于到期重新谈判。华住年报对其租赁酒店的描述是，租约通常允许经双方同意后延期。
法律给的两项安排也不等于续租权。《民法典》第七百三十四条第二款规定，房屋承租人享有以同等条件优先承租的权利。“同等条件”是说，出租人准备按某个租金租给别人时，你可以按同样条件先租；它不锁定租金，出租人不再出租时也用不上。
第七百三十四条第一款处理的是另一种情形：租赁期限届满，承租人继续使用，出租人没有提出异议的，原租赁合同继续有效，但是租赁期限为不定期。不定期，就是没有终止日期。第七百三十条对视为不定期的租赁写明，当事人可以随时解除合同，但应当在合理期限之前通知对方；期满续用形成的不定期租赁，一般也按这个规则理解。在这种状态下继续投钱装修，回收期没有年限可以依托。
会计口径可作参照。华住财报附注写明，续租选择权只有在集团合理确定会行使时，才计入使用权资产和租赁负债。使用权资产，是承租人对租来物业在租期内使用权的入账价值。上市公司记账尚且只计入合理确定的续租，单店测算的基准也应采用同样的保守口径。
## 装修投下去，到期能拿回多少？
先分清两类投入。一类可以带走，比如活动家具、可拆运的设备和系统。另一类与房屋结合在一起，拆下来就坏或不值钱，比如吊顶、墙地面、固定管线和卫生间防水，法律上称为“附合”。
《民法典》第七百一十五条规定，承租人经出租人同意，可以对租赁物进行改善或者增设他物；未经同意的，出租人可以请求恢复原状或者赔偿损失。“经出租人同意”是前提，同意应当落在书面上。

到期怎么处理，看租赁司法解释第八至十一条。第八条：经同意的装修，租期届满或合同解除时，没有附合的部分，除另有约定外可由承租人拆除，拆坏房屋要恢复原状。第十条：承租人经出租人同意装饰装修，租赁期间届满时，请求出租人补偿附合装饰装修费用的，不予支持，但当事人另有约定的除外。第九条处理中途解除，前提是双方对附合部分怎么处理没有约定：因出租人违约解除的，承租人请求赔偿剩余租赁期内装饰装修残值损失，应予支持；因承租人违约解除的，不予支持，但出租人同意利用的，应在利用价值范围内适当补偿。第十一条：未经同意装修或扩建的费用由承租人负担。
换成钱来说，附合的装修如果合同没有另行约定补偿，到期价值按零算，只能靠租期内的经营现金流收回。华住财报对租赁物业改良，即在租来的房子里做的装修和改造，折旧年限写的是租赁期与预计使用年限孰短。装修能用十五年，租约只剩八年，就按八年摊完。
## 怎样用剩余租期检查回收期？
回收期，指从投入发生起，到扣除租金后的累计经营净现金流收回全部投入所需的年数。它能说明钱多久回来，不能说明回来之后赚多少，也不反映资金的时间成本。所以它只适合作底线检查，不能代替内部收益率测算。
测算里的租金要按合同递增条款逐年写入。华住披露的常见安排是：起租时有两到八个月免租期，前三到五年租金固定，之后每三到五年上调2%至6%。这是一家集团的条款范围，不能当作行业标准。
下面这张表，可以在签约、追加改造或谈转让价之前填一次。表中示例数字均为假设。

| 核对项 | 去哪里取证 | 示例（假设） | 怎样进测算 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 合同到期日 | 租赁合同及补充协议，超过二十年的部分不计 | 还剩10年 | 基准年限的上限 |
| 出租人最早可收回日 | 提前终止、征收、出租人自用条款 | 第7年末可收回 | 与合同到期日取较早者 |
| 出租人自身权利 | 产权证、规划许可、抵押登记时间，二房东的上手租约 | 上手租约还剩9年 | 与前两项取较早者 |
| 续租 | 单方选择权、协商续签，还是只有优先承租权 | 协商续签 | 只进情景，不进基准 |
| 装修与复原 | 附合装修有无补偿约定，复原标准和费用 | 不补偿，复原费100万元 | 投入在可执行年限内收回，复原费列为到期支出 |
按表中假设推演：改造投入2400万元，改造期1年，开业第一年净现金流250万元，此后每年400万元。累计到第7年末，还差150万元，第8年才收回。合同还剩10年，看起来能回本；按可执行的7年算，出租人第7年末收回，再付复原费100万元，这个项目亏250万元，除非合同约定提前收回时按剩余租期补偿装修残值。
判断规则是：把复原费用计入投入后算出的回收期，应短于可执行的剩余租期，并留出余量。余量多大由投委会按项目风险定，本文不给统一数字。续租后的年份另做一个情景，回答续上了能多赚多少，不用来回答能不能投。
## 剩余租期怎样压住估值？
收购或转让一家租赁经营的酒店，买方买到的是剩余租期内的经营权和可以带走的设备，不包括房屋。卖方常拿已投的装修额要价。按租赁司法解释第十条，附合装修到期一般不获补偿，它对买方的价值只体现在剩余年限的现金流里。
用年净现金流乘一个倍数来估值，隐含的前提是现金流能持续足够多年。仍用假设：可执行的剩余租期5年，每年净现金流400万元，到期复原费100万元，不折现的现金流合计也只有1900万元。若按8倍报价3200万元，多出的1300万元只能靠续租兑现。倍数能说明市场对一类资产的定价习惯，不能说明这一份租约还剩几年。
## 什么情况下可以放宽，什么情况下该停？
有三种情况，年限约束可以放宽。一是出租人承担主体装修：华住披露，旗下德意志酒店集团的部分酒店由出租人负责除软装以外的装修，承租方带不走的投入少，对年限的依赖就小。二是合同约定提前收回时按剩余年限补偿装修残值，而且出租人有支付能力。三是续租写成承租人单方选择权，租金有公式，续订期限不超过二十年。
出现下列任一情况，应暂停签约或追加投入：计入复原费用后的回收期长于可执行的剩余租期；出租人拿不出产权证或规划许可；抵押登记早于租约，抵押权人的态度说不清；转租链上任何一环的剩余租期短于测算年限；租约已经到期，处于不定期状态。
分工要先定。法务出具可执行剩余租期的书面意见，写明每个截断日期的依据；工程把投入拆成可带走和附合两张清单；财务按可执行年限做基准测算，续租单列情景；投委会或业主定余量并拍板。做没做到位，看测算表里的基准年限能否逐项对上合同和权属文件。签约后每年复核一次：可执行剩余租期还剩几年，未收回的投入还要几年收回。前者短于后者，就停止追加投入，先谈延长租期或补偿条款。
本文讨论境内城镇房屋租赁，是投资测算的组织方法，不能替代具体项目的法律意见。业主自持物业的酒店不受租期约束，但仍要按资产寿命测算。迈创兄弟C&T可以协助把租约条款和这张测算表对齐。

contentEn: When a hotel operates in leased premises, the renovation investment has to be recovered within the enforceable remaining lease term. A renewal belongs in a scenario, not in the base case. Valuation is bound by the same limit: when a buyer acquires only the operating rights and not the building, the price it is willing to pay should not exceed the cash flow it can obtain over those years, less the cost of restoring the premises at expiry. The number of years left on the contract is only the starting point.

This is often done the wrong way round. An investment committee first calculates the payback period and only then checks whether the lease is long enough, or it hears the landlord say "we'll definitely renew with you" and counts the years after renewal as well. A landlord's verbal assurance, a letter of intent and statements reported in the press are background material only, not binding. Only terms written into the contract count.
## Why is the lease term in the contract not the same as the years you can actually use?

First, separate two concepts. The contractual lease term is the start and end date stated in the lease. The enforceable remaining lease term is the number of years from today to the earliest date on which the tenant could be forced to leave. The second is often shorter.

The first cap comes from the law. Article 705 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China states: "The term of a lease shall not exceed twenty years. Where it exceeds twenty years, the excess part is invalid." The lease may be renewed at expiry, but the renewed term also may not exceed twenty years from the date of renewal. If the contract says thirty years, the model can only count twenty.

The second comes from the contract. H World Group states in its 2025 annual report that its leases typically provide that they could be terminated under certain legal or factual conditions. Once a clause on expropriation, repossession by the landlord or redevelopment could be triggered, the enforceable term ends on that date.

The third comes from the landlord's own rights. Under Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Urban Housing Lease Contracts (2020 Amendment, the "Lease Interpretation"), a lease signed by a landlord for a building that has no construction project planning permit, or was not built in accordance with its permit, is invalid, unless the permit is obtained before the close of court debate at first instance. Article 14 provides that where a mortgage was created on the building before it was let, and ownership changes because the mortgagee enforces the mortgage, a tenant's claim that the new owner must continue to perform the original lease will not be upheld, unless otherwise agreed.

If the landlord itself holds the property under a lease, acting as a sublessor (colloquially a "second landlord" in China), Article 717 of the Civil Code provides that the part of a sublease term that exceeds the sublessor's remaining lease term is not legally binding on the original landlord, unless otherwise agreed. H World also notes among its risk factors that some of its lessors have failed to provide property ownership certificates or land use rights certificates, so the relevant leases may be invalidated and the hotels may have to relocate.
## Renewal clauses, the preferential right to lease and leases of indefinite term: how much does each secure?

Contract wording about "renewal" varies widely in strength. Where the tenant can decide unilaterally to renew and the rent is set by an agreed formula, it is a renewal option, the closest thing to certainty. Wording that only says "the parties will negotiate a renewal" amounts to starting negotiations again at expiry. H World's annual report describes its leased hotels this way: its leases usually allow extensions by mutual agreement.

Two arrangements under the law are not renewal rights either. Paragraph 2 of Article 734 of the Civil Code gives the tenant of a building a preferential right to lease on equal terms. "Equal terms" means that if the landlord intends to let the property to someone else at a certain rent, you can lease it first on the same terms. It does not lock in the rent, and it does not help if the landlord stops letting the property.

Paragraph 1 of Article 734 deals with a different situation: where the lease term has expired, the tenant continues to use the property and the landlord raises no objection, the original lease remains valid, but it becomes a lease of indefinite term. An indefinite term means there is no end date. For leases deemed to be of indefinite term, Article 730 states that either party may terminate the contract at any time, provided it gives the other party notice a reasonable time in advance. A lease of indefinite term created by continued use after expiry is generally understood to follow the same rule. In this state, if you keep spending on fit-out, the payback period has no fixed number of years to rely on.

Accounting practice offers a reference point. The notes to H World's financial statements state that lease extension options are included in right-of-use assets and lease liabilities only to the extent that it is reasonably certain the Group will exercise them. A right-of-use asset is the recognised value of a lessee's right to use leased property during the lease term. If even a listed company's accounts include only renewals that are reasonably certain, the base case for a single hotel should take the same conservative approach.
## Once the fit-out money is spent, how much comes back at expiry?

First, distinguish two kinds of investment. One kind can be taken away, such as loose furniture, and equipment and systems that can be dismantled and relocated. The other is joined to the building and is ruined or worthless once removed, such as ceilings, wall and floor finishes, fixed piping and cabling, and bathroom waterproofing. In law, fit-out of this kind is said to have become attached to the building, a concept known as accession.

Article 715 of the Civil Code provides that a tenant may, with the landlord's consent, improve the leased property or add other things to it. Without consent, the landlord may require the tenant to restore it to its original condition or pay compensation. "With the landlord's consent" is the precondition, and the consent should be put in writing.

What happens at expiry is governed by Articles 8 to 11 of the Lease Interpretation. Article 8: for fit-out carried out with consent, when the lease expires or is terminated, the tenant may remove the parts that have not become attached, unless otherwise agreed, and must restore the building if removal damages it. Article 10: where a tenant carries out fit-out with the landlord's consent and, when the lease term expires, asks the landlord to compensate it for the cost of attached fit-out, the claim will not be upheld, unless the parties have agreed otherwise. Article 9 covers termination before expiry, where the parties have not agreed how attached fit-out is to be dealt with: if the lease is terminated because of the landlord's breach, the tenant's claim for loss of the residual value of the fit-out over the remaining lease term should be upheld; if it is terminated because of the tenant's breach, the claim will not be upheld, but if the landlord agrees to use the fit-out, it should pay appropriate compensation within the value of that use. Article 11: the cost of fit-out or extension carried out without consent is borne by the tenant.

In money terms, unless the contract separately provides for compensation, attached fit-out should be valued at zero at expiry and can be recovered only through operating cash flow during the lease. For leasehold improvements, meaning the fit-out and alterations made in a leased building, H World's financial statements set the depreciation period at the shorter of the lease term or their estimated useful lives. If the fit-out could last fifteen years but the lease has only eight left, it is depreciated in full over eight years.
## How do you test the payback period against the remaining lease term?

The payback period is the number of years from when the investment is made until cumulative net operating cash flow after rent recovers the whole investment. It shows how soon the money comes back, not how much is earned afterwards, and it ignores the time cost of capital. So it is suitable only as a minimum check and cannot replace an internal rate of return calculation.

Rent in the model should be entered year by year according to the escalation clauses in the contract. The common arrangement H World discloses is a rent-free period of two to eight months at the start, fixed rent for the first three to five years, and then an increase of 2% to 6% every three to five years. This is the range of terms at one group and should not be treated as an industry standard.
The table below can be filled in once before signing, before spending more on renovation, or before negotiating a transfer price. All example figures in the table are assumptions.

| Item to check | Where to find the evidence | Example (assumed) | How it enters the model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contract expiry date | The lease and any supplementary agreements; any part beyond twenty years is not counted | 10 years remaining | Upper limit of the base-case term |
| Landlord's earliest repossession date | Clauses on early termination, expropriation and the landlord's own use | Can be repossessed at the end of year 7 | Take the earlier of this and the contract expiry date |
| Landlord's own rights | Title certificate, planning permit and mortgage registration date; a second landlord's head lease | 9 years left on the head lease | Take the earliest of this and the two items above |
| Renewal | A unilateral option, a negotiated renewal, or only a preferential right to lease | Negotiated renewal | Scenario only, not the base case |
| Fit-out and restoration | Whether compensation for attached fit-out has been agreed; the restoration standard and cost | No compensation; restoration cost of RMB 1 million | Recover the investment within the enforceable term; treat restoration as a cost at expiry |

Working through the assumptions in the table: a renovation investment of RMB 24 million, a one-year renovation period, net cash flow of RMB 2.5 million in the first year of operation and RMB 4 million a year after that. By the end of year 7 the project is still RMB 1.5 million short, and it pays back only in year 8. With 10 years left on the contract, it appears to pay back. On the enforceable term of 7 years, however, the landlord takes the property back at the end of year 7, the tenant pays RMB 1 million in restoration, and the project loses RMB 2.5 million, unless the contract provides that on early repossession the fit-out is compensated for its residual value over the remaining term.

The rule is this: the payback period, calculated with restoration costs counted as part of the investment, should be shorter than the enforceable remaining lease term, with a margin to spare. The size of the margin should be set by the investment committee according to the project's risk, and this article does not give a single figure. The years after renewal go into a separate scenario, which answers how much more could be earned if the lease is renewed, not whether to invest.
## How does the remaining lease term cap valuation?

When a hotel operated under a lease is bought or sold, the buyer acquires the operating rights for the remaining lease term and the equipment that can be taken away, not the building. Sellers often base their asking price on the amount already spent on fit-out. Under Article 10 of the Lease Interpretation, attached fit-out is generally not compensated at expiry, so its value to the buyer lies only in the cash flow over the remaining years.

Valuing a hotel as a multiple of annual net cash flow implicitly assumes that the cash flow will last enough years. Again using assumptions: with an enforceable remaining term of 5 years, annual net cash flow of RMB 4 million and a restoration cost of RMB 1 million at expiry, total undiscounted cash flow is only RMB 19 million. At an asking price of RMB 32 million, 8 times annual net cash flow, the extra RMB 13 million can be realised only through renewal. A multiple shows how the market usually prices a type of asset. It cannot tell you how many years are left on this particular lease.
## When can the constraint be relaxed, and when should you stop?

The term constraint can be relaxed in three cases. First, the landlord pays for the main fit-out: H World discloses that at some of its Deutsche Hospitality hotels the landlords are responsible for renovation other than soft furnishings, so less of the tenant's investment is non-removable and the tenant depends less on the term. Second, the contract provides that on early repossession the fit-out is compensated for its residual value over the remaining term, and the landlord is able to pay. Third, renewal is written as a unilateral option for the tenant, with rent set by a formula and a renewed term of no more than twenty years.

Signing or further investment should be put on hold if any of the following applies: the payback period including restoration costs is longer than the enforceable remaining lease term; the landlord cannot produce a title certificate or planning permit; the mortgage was registered before the lease and the mortgagee's position is unclear; any link in the sublease chain has a remaining term shorter than the modelled term; or the lease has already expired and become a lease of indefinite term.

Assign responsibilities up front. Legal provides a written opinion on the enforceable remaining lease term, stating the basis for each cut-off date. Engineering splits the investment into two lists, removable and attached. Finance builds the base case on the enforceable term and models renewal as a separate scenario. The investment committee or the owner sets the margin and makes the decision. To check whether this has been done properly, see whether the base-case term in the model can be matched item by item to the contract and title documents. After signing, review once a year: how many years remain on the enforceable lease term, and how many more years it will take to recover the outstanding investment. If the first is shorter than the second, stop further investment and negotiate a longer lease or compensation terms first.

This article covers urban building leases in mainland China and sets out a way to organise investment modelling. It does not replace legal advice on a specific project. Hotels in properties the owner owns outright are not constrained by a lease term, but should still be modelled on the life of the asset.
